newsitem.title: UK: UK's Hague says budget breaks Labour tax vow.
newsitem.headline: UK's Hague says budget breaks Labour tax vow.

text.p: The budget introduced on Wednesday by Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown breaks pledges made by the Labour Party during the election campaign not to raise the tax burden, Conservative leader William Hague said.

"When the Prime Minister (Tony Blair) said before the election, and I quote, "We've no plans to increase tax at all', he did not mean a word of it," Hague told parliament in his speech responding to Brown's proposals.
"This is a tax raising budget. When the Chancellor says he is tightening fiscal policy by 5-3/4 billion (pounds), he means he is introducing a tax raising budget."
"Why were these proposals not made clear before that general election?" -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
